title: Data Structures & Algorithms
blurb: The path from Big-O to dynamic programming and interview performance, ordered by how you should learn it. Each pattern node has real problems; do the must-do nodes first, the rest can wait.

title: Backend Engineer
blurb: What a backend engineer should know, in the order to learn it: HTTP and OS basics, Node.js and TypeScript in depth, SQL and NoSQL, APIs, auth and security, caching, messaging, testing, architecture, DevOps, observability, system design and interview prep.
audience: Developers aiming for a backend or backend-heavy full-stack role

title: Frontend Engineer
blurb: What a frontend engineer should know, in the order to learn it: the browser, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, accessibility, TypeScript, React and Next.js, state and data, testing, performance, security, tooling, frontend system design and interview prep.
audience: Developers aiming for a frontend or UI-heavy full-stack role

title: Senior Frontend: scaling the frontend
blurb: For engineers going from mid to senior or staff: rendering and state architecture at scale, design systems, monorepos, micro-frontends, performance, testing strategy, frontend infrastructure, safe releases, security, i18n and leading frontend architecture.
audience: Mid-level frontend engineers aiming for senior or staff roles

title: Full-Stack Engineer
blurb: Frontend, backend, data, deployment and AI features tied together: the web platform, HTML/CSS, TypeScript, React and Next.js, APIs, Node, Postgres and MongoDB, auth, caching and queues, testing, DevOps, observability and system design.
audience: Developers aiming for full-stack product engineering roles

title: AI Engineer (GenAI end to end)
blurb: The deepest AI-engineering tier: beyond the syllabus AI track and Web lessons into fine-tuning, MLOps, evals, safety, serving and cost, plus portfolio and career prep. Use GenAI sprint (/genai-sprint) for a 45-day plan with done-when checks; it never affects your streak.
audience: Software engineers moving into AI engineering or GenAI product roles

title: GenAI Engineer: the 16-level roadmap
blurb: Sixteen levels from software fundamentals to a full mock interview loop, with every module and topic of the CampusX AI Engineering Roadmap (286 sessions), a capstone per level and free resources. Must-do is Levels 0 to 10 and 15; Levels 11 to 14 are can-do. Never touches your streak.
audience: Software engineers moving into AI engineering and GenAI product roles

title: GenAI in 100 days (accelerated)
blurb: The CampusX 100 Days of AI Engineering route: 6 modules, 86 day-units, then 12 portfolio projects and 100 interview questions with what a strong answer covers. Each unit has topics, a try-it task and an outcome. Skipped topics point to the 16-level roadmap.
audience: Engineers who know basic Python, APIs and Git and want the shortest path to shipping AI apps

title: GenAI Interview Playbook
blurb: The 23-week plan from Oct 26 2026 to Mar 31 2027: Python and SQL, LLM and RAG internals, agents, production, system design and mocks, each week ending in a proof artifact.
audience: Software engineers preparing for AI engineer interviews
